subject: Recap: 10-day validation sprint & parity probes
summary: Post-call recap capturing HelixCare's top pains (latency, cost, hallucination), decision criteria, and an assigned 10-day validation sprint with parity probes and owners.
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@helixcare.com>, Dana Schultz <dana.schultz@healthx.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: 10-day validation sprint & parity probes

Hi Sanjay / Dana  thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Top pains you called out:
- High tail latency on multi-turn summarization (spikes >1s on peak traffic).
- Token cost is material at current volumes; looking for ~30% unit-cost improvement.
- Occasional hallucinations on clinical-note extraction that need measurable regression tests.
- Regulatory concern: audit logs + data residency controls for PHI.

Goals you prioritized:
1) Reduce average inference latency to <200ms for single-turn inference and tighten 95th percentile.
2) 30% improvement in per-token cost versus current vendor under realistic load.
3) Validated hallucination reduction on your sample dataset (scored and reproducible).
4) Evidence of audit logging and KMS support for an on-prem/private deployment if needed.

Decision criteria (agreed):
- Latency under target across 3 traffic shapes
- Cost per 1M tokens at scale
- Security/compliance posture (SOC2 controls, audit logs)
- Ease of integration (prefix caching, SDKs)

Open questions we recorded:
- Which dataset/version should we use for hallucination regression? (Sanity & clinical edge cases)
- Minimum acceptable throughput requirement (tokens/sec) for your ingestion pipeline?
- Will you want a Dedicated pool or Private deployment for the pilot?

Proposed 10-day validation sprint (high level):
- Day 0: Kickoff + share datasets and access
- Days 1–3: Latency & throughput smoke tests (three traffic shapes) — owner: Rishi
- Days 4–6: Cost simulation & batching/quantization experiments — owner: Camila
- Days 7–9: Hallucination regression & scoring on your sample set — owner: Lauren/Camila
- Day 10: Readout + go/no-go recommendation and next procurement steps

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Sanjay: confirm which dataset (A/B/C) we should use for hallucination tests by EOD Tuesday.
- Dana: confirm minimum throughput requirement and any non-negotiable compliance items.
- Redwood (Camila/Rishi): circulate the detailed sprint plan and vendor parity matrix by tomorrow.

I attached a short probe outline to this email: redwood-probe-outline.pdf (high-level tests and measurement plan).

Thanks again  we can start the sprint as soon as we have the dataset and throughput numbers.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0119
Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren  this is great and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Priority order: 1) compliance/auditability, 2) latency stability, 3) cost — we need the audit log samples early so our compliance team can review.
- For hallucination tests we'll provide Dataset-B (de-identified clinical notes) — I'll share secure access later today.
- Throughput: baseline currently ~120 reqs/sec for the summarization pipeline; peak bursts up to ~400.

Also, would like to include one of our security engineers (cc'd Dana) on the sprint kickoff — there are a couple of SOC2 controls we want validated as part of the run. Attached the SOC-related asks we typically use: helixcare-soc2-ask.xlsx.

If you can confirm the kickoff time/window tomorrow, we'll lock it in.

Appreciate the clear plan — Sanjay

Subject: Re: Recap: 10-day validation sprint & parity probes — technical probes / test assignments

Looping in technical detail for the sprint. High-level test matrix below (we'll expand in the Drive doc):

1) Latency probes (owner: Rishi)
- Shapes: single-turn small prompt, multi-turn summarization (10-turns), streaming token-by-token.
- Metrics: mean, p50, p95, p99, cold-start 1st-token.
- Smoke config: batch sizes [1,4,8], sequence lengths [128,512,2048].

2) Cost simulation (owner: Camila)
- Run real-volume token generation on model variants: float32 baseline, q4-bit, q8_0 variants.
- Measure tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens after batching and prefix cache enabled.

3) Hallucination regression (owner: Lauren/Camila)
- Use Dataset-B (de-identified) with labelled ground truth. Output scored by ROUGE/F1 + clinician spot-checks.
- Save outputs and seed for reproducibility.

4) Parity matrix
- We'll run the same tests across three candidates: current vendor vX, Redwood-default model, Redwood-quantized variant.
- Produce a vendor parity matrix and highlight regressions.

Action items I can take right away:
- Produce the initial test harness and a containerized runner by tomorrow AM (linking to Drive doc).
- Provide sample workloads that match your burst profile.

I'll publish the technical README and the parity spreadsheet to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helix-probes

Rishi Malhotra
Lead ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
